news.headline: Gold slips for a third session as yields and oil-led inflation fears weigh
news.summary: Spot fell as low as ~$4,115-4,127 in early Asia (Reuters, Kitco range) before recovering to ~$4,141 (Kitco 08:43 IST); Monday -0.6%. Brent above $109 keeps inflation and a restrictive Fed in focus.

news.headline: US yields climb: 10Y 5.14%, 2Y 4.78%, 30Y 5.48% as oil fuels inflation worries
news.summary: Treasury yields rose 3-6bp Monday, reversing part of last week's rally; higher yields lift gold's opportunity cost.

news.headline: FedWatch: 83% October hold, ~94% December hike
news.summary: Fed in blackout; markets lean to an October pause but a December hike is nearly fully priced after 3.7% CPI. FXStreet shows 82.8% hold.

news.headline: Houthis claim strikes on Aramco Yanbu, Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh and Abha airports
news.summary: Saudi authorities did not confirm; Brent hit $110.70 Monday (highest since 20-May) before easing to ~$109. Gulf infrastructure risk keeps a haven bid but also feeds inflation and yields.

news.headline: Lavrov in Tehran links Hormuz reopening to guarantees for Iran; strait still disrupted
news.summary: Russia backs the June US-Iran MoU as a basis; Iran wants the US to accept the Iran-Oman strait deal. Trump vows to "finish the job"; US and Iranian strikes continue.

news.headline: French spread hits 147bp, widest since 2011-12, as riots bring curfews
news.summary: Partial curfews in Paris; PM Lecornu vows to restore order. EUR steady ~1.1215 after Monday dip. Euro-area stress supports haven demand but can lift the dollar.

news.headline: Oil eases on possible Russia sanctions waiver; WTI Nov expires Tuesday
news.summary: Brent ~$109 (from $110.70 high); Trump waiver order not final per Rubio. IEA: Russian output +65k bpd in September.

synthesis.overnight_summary: Gold lost ~0.6% on Monday as Brent touched $110.70 on Houthi strikes against Saudi energy sites and US yields rebounded ~6bp (10Y 5.14%), leaving spot ~$4,140 at the MCX close; MCX Dec ended at 147,302 (-616), near its low. Early Asia extended the slide to ~$4,115-4,127 on Kospi's 3.6% AI-led drop and BoJ hawkishness, but dip-buying returned spot to ~$4,141 by 08:43 IST, essentially flat versus the MCX close. With the onshore rupee closed for Dussehra, the only quote (offshore-indicative 95.24 vs 94.91 close) adds ~Rs 505, putting model fair value near Rs 147839 (+537) - almost all of it currency, so it is low-confidence. MCX trades only from 17:00 IST today; the reopen will hinge on spot holding $4,135 and on US yields and oil into the evening.
